H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in Terry v. Ohio (1968) did not establish that evidence obtained through unlawful searches is strictly inadmissible in state criminal trials under the Fourth Amendment exclusionary rule. In fact, the Court in Terry v. Ohio held that the revolver seized from Terry was properly admitted in evidence against him, as the search was reasonable under the circumstances. The exclusionary rule was already established in Mapp v. Ohio (1961), which held that evidence obtained through unlawful searches is inadmissible in state criminal trials. Terry v. Ohio dealt with the reasonableness of a stop and frisk, not the exclusionary rule itself. (Case ID: 392_0001-01)
